author: 5kO0
content:
Source: external technical review by the jacquard atproto SDK author (separate Rust impl). Investigated each claim against the actual codebase 2026-05-08; full audit transcript in this session's history.

Verdicts: 7 of 7 substantive claims confirmed (full or partial). One claim originally tagged "REFUTED" by an Explore subagent was re-evaluated and found partially valid (ciborium leniency on decode path).

Meta-goal: this epic is the substrate for proto-blue surpassing both the TS reference SDK and jacquard. The reviewer surfaced the proof-pipeline test gap (L2) explicitly so we could close it; that's the highest-leverage finding because the TS reference itself has been observed emitting invalid sync v1.1 commits with insufficient blocks for the proof. Property/fuzz coverage on covering_proof + a slight-overestimate strategy (à la tranquil-pds) is the path to spec-correct emission proto-blue can ship and the TS suite cannot.

Order of attack (suggested):
  L2  critical  proof-pipeline tests              — silent-correctness; differentiator
  L3  high      codegen newtypes                  — propagates to whole API
  L5  high      codegen edition-2024 keywords     — latent compile breakage
  L4  high      codegen union sum types
  L6  high      Agent public surface uses syntax newtypes
  L7  medium    Cid → cid crate
  L8  medium    serde_ipld_dagcbor migration
  L9  medium    decode_lenient float coercion
  L10 medium    interop diff expansion
  L11 medium    real-world lexicon corpus test

L3+L4+L5 ideally land together since they all reshape codegen output and re-running gen is cheap. L6 should land after L3 so the Agent migration consumes the new types directly.
